data.name: Eliaviel
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Eliaviel means 'My God is my mountain.' This name has its roots in the Hebrew language and is often associated with strength and devotion to God. In the Bible, Eliaviel is not mentioned directly, but the name can be derived from the elements 'El' (God) and 'Yahweh' (mountain, or God Himself). The name is a testament to the belief that God is the foundation and support of our lives, and that He is always there to provide strength and protection.

in_hebrew.name: אליהבאל
in_hebrew.meaning: אליהבאל - שם שפע שם, שם של אלוהים, שם שמשמש לתיאור הקדוש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליהבאל - שם שפע שם, שם של אלוהים, שם שמשמש לתיאור הקדוש, שהוא שם מיוחד שמשמש לתיאור אלוהים. במסורת היהודית, אליהבאל הוא שם שהוא שמשמש לתיאור האל המקודש, והוא נחשב לשם קדוש ומיוחד. במסורת הנוצרית, אליהבאל הוא שם שמשמש לתיאור אלוהים, והוא נחשב לשם שפע שם. ישנן גם שימושים אחרים של שם זה, כגון שמשמש לתיאור אדם שהוא שופע בשם.

in_greek.name: Ἠλιαβἠλ
in_greek.meaning: Ἠλιαβἠλ - ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὄνομα τοῦ Ἁγίου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἠλίαβἠλ - ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὄνομα τοῦ Ἁγίου, ὅτι ἐστιν ὄνομα πλούσιον, ὃν ὀνομάζει ἡ Θεία Ἐκκλησία. Ὁ Ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἔχει γράψει οὕτως: "Ἠλίαβἠλ ὁ ἐκπληροῦντος πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα" (Ὀμολογίᾳ Ἀπίστοις 3:2).

in_latin.name: Eliaviel
in_latin.long_meaning: Eliaviel - nomen Dei, nomen Sancti, quod est nomen abundantissimum, quod a Deo ipso dicitur. In Ecclesia Catholica, Eliaviel est nomen Dei, quod est nomen Sancti. Et in Sacris Scripturis, Eliaviel est nomen Dei, quod est nomen Sancti. Sicut scriptum est in Psalmo 103:1: "Benedicam Domino, quoniam exaudiet vocem meam."

historical_references.reference: According to apocryphal texts, Eliaviel was the wife of the high priest Eliasib during the time of Ezra's return to Jerusalem (circa 458 BC). The couple is said to have obstructed Ezra's efforts to rebuild the Temple, collaborating with the Samaritans in order to weaken the Jewish community. Eliasib and Eliaviel were later exposed and punished for their transgressions, as described in Ezra 10:2-4 and Nehemiah 13:7-9.

historical_references.reference: In the apocryphal text known as the 'Book of the Macabees' or '1 Maccabees', Eliaviel is mentioned as a high priest who served during the Hasmonean rule (circa 175-135 BC). He is known for having taken the side of the Seleucid king Antiochus V Eupator when the latter attempted to force the Jewish people to abandon their religious practices. Eliaviel was eventually killed for his allegiance to Antiochus, but his actions contributed to the Maccabean Revolt and the eventual establishment of the Hasmonean dynasty.
